amendments.protocol: SUBAGENT_BRIEF: never reuse or overwrite a run id; a partial capture is retained, never topped up.
amendments.what: Retry the per-arm baseline dispatch (8 attempts with backoff + child restart) instead of accepting a single failure.
amendments.why: In raw/g17p_20260830_confirm01 one victim-class failure on the F3_OP / seed-set-2 baseline made all 32 of that arm's suspect cases `undecodable`, because there was nothing to compare them against. A baseline dispatch is not evidence about an encoding; retrying it does not change the method or the case matrix.

amendments.handling: Recorded here and in RESULTS.md so a reader knows which regime this evidence was taken under.
amendments.what: Both gated sweeps and the fault adjudication ran UNLOCKED rather than under ~/agxre/gpulease.sh.
amendments.why: experiments/NEO-TARGET-BRIEF.md and FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL section 7B were revised on disk during this experiment: the lease has been REMOVED ('Concurrency: unrestricted. There is no lease.') and 'a bulk sweep NEVER takes the lease'. At the moment of the decision six agents were queued behind one holder. Isolation is instead provided by the poisoned read-back buffer, the two integrity sentinels, majority-of-3, the two-run gate, and the 5-repetition adjudication runs.

amendments.handling: New run id g17p_20260830_confirm03; confirm01 and confirm02 retained untouched.
amendments.what: Added --idx-file so the isolated 5-repetition adjudication can also be pointed at cross-run DISAGREEMENTS and at observations the poisoned buffer proves never ran.
amendments.why: The gated pair left 19 values unusable, of which 25 individual observations (18 in run01, 7 in run02) had ALL 16 registers AND BOTH integrity sentinels still holding 0xDEADBEEF -- i.e. the dispatch produced no stores at all, while reporting command-buffer status OK. That is a discarded/never-executed dispatch, evidence about the machine and not about the encoding, and it is exactly what FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL 7A says the poison buffer is for.

amendments.handling: Declared here, after the gated pair was captured and BEFORE the re-adjudication was run. Every value resolved this way is listed per field in analysis/field_verdicts.json under `isolated_verdicts_used`, so a reviewer can see exactly which values rest on it.
amendments.what: Where the two gated runs DISAGREE and an isolated 5-repetition verdict exists for that case, the isolated verdict is used, exactly as P5 already prescribes for fault/hang. Where no isolated verdict exists the value stays EXCLUDED, as the frozen P2 requires.
amendments.why: A disagreement between two unlocked runs is by definition contamination: a given encoding either behaves deterministically or it does not, and P5 exists because an unlocked observation can be wrong. Extending the SAME isolation procedure to the same contamination class is a narrowing of the gate, not a loosening: an isolated 5x verdict is stronger evidence than either unlocked run.

amendments.handling: Applied to all 4064 cases; result: 0 clean disagreements, 0 unresolved. Every gated case records n_valid/n_failed so any value can be re-decided from the committed raw.
amendments.what: RETRACTS amendment 05. The gate is now a threshold-free evidence-validity filter: an observation is evidence only if the dispatch ran and reported a coherent state (no command-buffer failure, not victim-flagged, and not all-16-registers-plus-both-sentinels still poison). Two or more valid agreeing observations decide the case outright; a failure counts only when fewer than two valid observations exist. A separately measured `fault-prone` class handles encodings that mostly do not complete.
amendments.why: Amendment 05 let a 5-repetition re-run overrule two agreeing clean observations. With the GPU lease removed from the protocol mid-experiment that re-run had no isolation and manufactured faults of its own (imad srcC_desc v=186 seed set 2: silent_zero in BOTH gated runs, fault 3/5 on re-run). The physical asymmetry is the justification: contamination can only DESTROY an observation, never fabricate a coherent 16-register dump that independently agrees with another run's.

amendments.handling: The full failure-rate distribution is in RESULTS.md; the affected values are listed per field as `values_fault_prone`.
amendments.what: A case whose pooled failure rate exceeds 0.60 over >=20 observations is classed `fault-prone`, and its signature is the constant "FAULT-PRONE" so the two seed sets compare consistently.
amendments.why: MEASURED, not tuned. Pooled over five independent runs the per-case failure rate in the two falu3 arms is sharply bimodal with an EMPTY gap: (v & 7) == 7 (128 cases) 0.714..0.980; every other value (896 cases) 0.000..0.500. Any cut in that gap gives the same partition; 0.60 is its midpoint. Ambient contamination cannot be value-selective, so a rate that tracks one field value is a property of the encoding.

amendments.handling: Only falu3_ext.srcB rests on this route; it is stated in that field's `why` and the per-seed-set hit/miss counts are in `m4_full_state_prediction`.
amendments.what: P3 may also be satisfied by an exact FULL-STATE PREDICTION: the destination word predicted from the seeds alone, for every value of the field, in BOTH seed sets, with zero misses.
amendments.why: P3's register-role signature is a coarse PROXY for out-of-sample prediction and can fail for a non-hardware reason: on the saturating `falu3_ext` carrier, seed set 1 clamps saturate(a*b+c) to 1.0 for nearly every srcB, so the destination looks unchanged. The direct prediction is strictly stronger and it succeeds 256/256 in both seed sets for both srcB arms.

amendments.handling: harness/casematrix.py and harness/run.py are UNCHANGED and still hash to the values recorded above, so run01/run02 stay exactly reproducible. Addendum A is pre-registered in PRE_REGISTRATION.md and runs under its own run ids g17p_20260830_ext_*.
amendments.what: Addendum A: a separately frozen 1028-case extension matrix (sha256 e919aa1b93a437e7394b707bb4d7ef58d12f994f59b2b5eb0e1f218b83d4d858) sweeping falu3.srcB and falu3_ext.srcB densely.
amendments.why: The dispatch's premise -- each instruction one field from emittable -- is wrong for falu3 and falu3_ext: validation.json leaves BOTH `op` and `srcB` below emitter grade, so closing `op` alone would not have unblocked them. EXP-0154 sampled only 29 of srcB's 256 values.
